cohort: 1,592 infants born at Muhimbili National Hospital, Tanzania
finding: Preliminary results from the Tanzanian Pulse Oximetry Study show a critical congenital heart disease detection rate of 2.5 per 1,000 live births and a pulse oximetry false positive rate of 0.6%, suggesting the acceptability of pulse oximetry screening for critical congenital heart disease in a well-prepared low resource setting.
